clinician.trajectory_summary: A 48-year-old man presented with 20 days of dizziness, nausea, vomiting, and 15 days of fever. Physical examination revealed sluggish light reflex and stiff neck (E004). Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis showed pleocytosis (cells 210 x 10^9/L), elevated protein (1371.5 mg/dL), and low glucose (1.1 mmol/L) (E002). Blood culture confirmed Listeria infection (E001). Cranial MRI showed lesions in the right pontine and brachium pontis (E003). Initial treatment included moxifloxacin, meropenem, and dexamethasone (E006). This was adjusted on day 3 to increased ampicillin (E011), and on day 4, meropenem and moxifloxacin were stopped, maintaining dexamethasone and ampicillin due to concerns about side effects (E012). By day 50 of hospitalization, the patient's consciousness returned to normal with normal blood routine (E020). There was a mention of a 'second admission' where intravenous anti-infection treatment with moxifloxacin and ampicillin was initiated (E027).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with symptoms including dizziness, nausea, vomiting, and fever, along with neurological signs of sluggish light reflex and stiff neck.
CSF analysis showed findings consistent with bacterial meningoencephalitis (pleocytosis, high protein, low glucose).
Cranial MRI revealed lesions in the right pontine and brachium pontis, indicating encephalitis.
Treatment regimen was adjusted to include ampicillin and dexamethasone, leading to clinical improvement.
